messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Using L-BFGS-B method with wlsmv estimator will be okay?
parts:
On 01/27/2015 04:56 PM, Seongho Bae wrote:
> Of course! Here you are!

Thanks.

I think the problems with nlminb() are related to the very small sample
size (N=263), compared to the large number of free parameters (257!).

Many two-way frequency tables have (many) empty cells. By default, if
the tables are larger than 2x2, lavaan will not do anything about, in
order not to distort the results. But in this case, I would recommend
adding a small constant to each empty cell, to stabilize the results:

fit <- cfa(mod_cfa_syntax, rawdata, estimator = 'wlsmv', ordered =
names(rawdata), verbose = T, zero.add=c(0.1, 0.1))

At least for the delta parameterization, this seems to give fairly
stable results. The theta parameterization still fails...

Would it be possible to collapse some response categories (ie merge them
together) in order to reduce the number of missing cells?

Yves.

After treating a lot of problems what you investigated with your great advices, I'll report the results again with attaching reproducible data and scripts.


Thanks again,

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Using L-BFGS-B method with wlsmv estimator will be okay?
parts:
On 02/16/2015 11:58 AM, Seongho Bae wrote:
> If can I reparameterize afterwards, How can I do that?

The standardized solutions should be the same under both
parameterizations. If you need to convert the raw (unstandardized)
parameters, you need a good understanding of how the parameterizations
work. See webnote 4 on the Mplus website for a good description.

Yves.
